clauses.reason: The order closes the listed agencies and excuses employees on two stated half days only, December 24 and December 31, 1953. It ended by its own terms at the close of December 31, 1953, the second and last day; the December 24 half day was spent at the close of that day. No later order is held that revokes, extends or amends it, and Executive Order 10358, cited for the meaning of holiday, is an earlier order that does not reach it.

research_rationale:
EO 10508 (signed 1953-12-14 by Dwight D. Eisenhower; filed 1953-12-15; 18 FR 8221, Federal Register of December 16, 1953 per the held source record) is read in full from the registered text jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_10508.recheck.txt (OCR with letter-spacing errors in its first lines; the whole order is present and its number, title and date agree with the census register). Inventory: one operative sentence with two joined commands limited to the same two days. First, the executive departments, independent establishments and other agencies in the metropolitan area of the District of Columbia, including the General Accounting Office, the Government Printing Office and the Navy Yard and Naval Stations, are closed one-half day on Thursday, December 24, 1953 and one-half day on Thursday, December 31, 1953. Second, federal employees in that area and in the field service, except those excluded for special public reasons or whose absence would conflict with existing law, are excused from duty on those half days, and each half day is a holiday within the meaning of Executive Order 10358 and of the statutes on compensation and leave. There is no recital, report deadline, extension or renewal clause. First end: by its own terms the order operates only on the two stated half days, so it was fully performed at the close of December 31, 1953, the later of the two; the December 24 half day was spent earlier. The text has no until-wording, so no inclusive or exclusive reading of an end date arises; the end is the last stated day. Later instruments: EO 10358 (June 9, 1952; held as actor context and read) predates this order, is cited only for its definition of holiday, and supersedes only EO 9636 (its section 8), so it cannot end this order; the dossier's missing line about EO 10358 and the one OFR-catalog hit concern that citation. A scan of every held order text for the bare number 10508 found only the order's own copies, the preceding order's text (which prints the same Federal Register contents), a codification-guide entry that lists 10358 with a see-EO-10508 pointer, and unrelated page numbers; none amends, extends or revokes it. Machine searches adopted after reading their coverage notes: current-law:usc (U.S. Code release point 119-121, citations of the order by number, edition through 2026-10-09, no hit), current-law:ecfr (eCFR as of 2026-10-14 and GovInfo CFR bulk, citations by number, no hit) and later-events:ofr_catalog (Office of the Federal Register disposition notes for 1937 onward plus operative sentences of saved order texts).

savings.reason: The order has no savings, pending-matter or continuing-effect wording. Pay and leave for the excused half days follow the compensation and leave statutes and Executive Order 10358, which the order invokes but does not extend, so nothing keeps the order operative after December 31, 1953.
